$comment: Session #5 closure gate manifest — the AUTHORITATIVE source of gate status and totals.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. PR #474 published '32 PASS · 6 BLOCKED · 1 NOT PROVEN' and PR #475
published '32 PASS · 7 BLOCKED · 0 NOT PROVEN', both over a declared denominator of 39.
Both aggregates were WRONG. The per-gate rows were individually correct, but the totals
were hand-maintained prose that nothing verified, and several markdown rows silently
carried more than one gate ('#467 · #468 · #469', 'Human / agent / pipelines ×3'). A
recount script written to check them had its own defect — it read '×3 shapes' out of an
EVIDENCE column as a gate multiplier — so the first correction attempt was also wrong.
The fix is structural, not a corrected number: every gate now has a permanent unique ID,
status lives in a machine-readable field, and scripts/session5ClosureGates.test.ts fails
the build if `totals` disagrees with `gates[]`, if an ID repeats, or if a status is not in
the allowed set. Markdown records must cite this file rather than maintain their own sums.
PASS        — requirement met at the stated evidence class.
BLOCKED     — an actual external authority restriction prevents execution. Never a defect.
NOT_PROVEN  — not established, and not blocked; e.g. a future window that has not occurred.
FAIL        — a real product or code defect. Never relabel a defect as BLOCKED.
EVIDENCE CLASSES: PROD (observed in production) | TEST (proven by a test shown to fail
against its defect) | INSPECT (read from shipped source or configuration) | NONE.
